short_description: The only animal in the atlas: an adult female Ixodes scapularis (blacklegged/deer tick), a hard tick (Ixodidae) with a fused body (idiosoma), no separate head, EIGHT legs, and barbed mouthparts on a forward capitulum. Vector, not a pathogen.
morphology_notes: Arachnid (Chelicerata), order Ixodida, family Ixodidae (hard ticks). Body plan: NO separate head — a fused idiosoma carries the whole body, with the mouthparts on a forward-projecting capitulum (gnathosoma).

EIGHT legs (four pairs) in the adult/nymph, all attaching to the anterior/front portion of the idiosoma. Only the six-legged LARVA has six legs — the target subject here is the adult/nymph, so eight legs is correct and mandatory.

Mouthparts on the capitulum: a barbed, harpoon-like HYPOSTOME (backward-pointing chitin barbs, anchors in skin, cement-coned during feeding) flanked by two CHELICERAE (cutting stylets that open the skin) and two leg-like sensory PALPS (do NOT pierce, sit alongside).

Hard tick (Ixodidae): a hardened dorsal plate, the SCUTUM, covers the WHOLE back in males (a 'conscutum') but only a small anterior shield in females/nymphs/larvae — which is exactly what lets the female idiosoma swell enormously when engorged with blood. Showing an unfed vs engorged female contrast is a strong teaching element.
Haller's organ: a pit-shaped sensory structure on the tarsus of the FIRST pair of legs, used to detect host heat, CO2 and odor while questing (forelegs raised).

Genus Ixodes is diagnostically EYELESS (no eyes on the scutum margins, unlike Dermacentor/Amblyomma), inornate (plain scutum, no pale ornamentation), lacks festoons (no scalloped rear-margin grooves), and has long, parallel-sided mouthparts.

Colour: reddish-brown to black; adult female has a dark anterior scutum/capitulum against a lighter red-brown abdomen; adult male is uniformly dark. This is real cuticle colour (not a false-colour convention).
do_not_draw: SIX legs (insect count) — must be EIGHT in the adult/nymph.
A separate insect-style head/thorax/abdomen segmentation — ticks have one fused idiosoma plus a capitulum, not a 3-part insect body.
A spider-like pinched narrow waist between two body regions — the idiosoma is one continuous oval, not two lobes on a pedicel.
Eyes on the scutum — Ixodes is an eyeless genus (diagnostic).
Festoons (scalloped rear-margin segments) — absent in Ixodes (present in other genera like Dermacentor).
A menacing/monstrous face or exaggerated fangs — keep it a neutral, accurate arachnid, not a horror-movie creature.
Blood/gore/bite-wound imagery on the teaching renders (textbook/sem/3d/watercolor) — anatomy only, no host skin trauma.
